scope: Cache-only dedicated actual NATS control fixture repair; source and gofmt only. No test/compiler/broker/engine execution.
changes: One original thirty-second fixture context starts before fixture acquisitions; it is canceled last by registered cleanup, not before owned controller cleanup. The actual request uses its two-second child context.

Dedicated broker owns CommandContext process and exclusive private log. Log cleanup registers immediately after Open; exact process cleanup registers immediately after Start before connection readiness.

Broker graceful SIGTERM targets only cmd.Process; sole Wait is checked. The only accepted nonzero reap is SIGKILL under expiry of the original fixture context, with no fresh cleanup timeout or adoption.

Each exact TLS dialer is retained in an immediate cleanup hook before Connect, including failed connect/Close. Raw dialer Close is checked before NATS Close; failed closes remain held for the exact registered retry.
Request goroutine has one joined result on all fatal paths; its actual returned TransportCleanupError is retained before assertions and its exact Close result is checked.
Input-free broker fixture creates no arbitrary output or engine authority; controlled inspection is still an explicit component seam.
limits: No actual cleanup failure injection or physically bounded unpreemptible Wait/Close proof.
Existing newBridgeFixture/control inspection preparation is reused; historical unchecked broker and raw TLS helpers are not called.
A terminal original-context SIGKILL proves exact process reaping, not why cancellation occurred.
